The email should earn a first evaluation of Senja for collecting student video testimony before a future cohort launch, without asserting an imminent recipient deadline. intent.reason_now: The selected audience's planning context is student video testimony for a future cohort launch; no recipient-specific launch date is established.
intent.desired_action: Start a free account to evaluate a student video collection and reuse workflow.

raw_plan.reader: A cohort-based course operator considering how to collect student video testimonials and use them on course or cohort sales pages.
raw_plan.reader_segment: A course creator or coach who needs student results on camera before the next cohort launch
raw_plan.reader_scope: Cohort-based course operators only. Solution-aware; installed tools, account ownership, collection history and launch dates remain unknown.
raw_plan.promise: Collect a student video testimonial in Senja, then view its automatic transcription and reuse the submitted video in a website widget.
raw_plan.orientation: For a small course or coaching team collecting student feedback for course and cohort sales pages, Senja is a tool for requesting text or video testimonials and displaying or reusing the responses.
raw_plan.arc: Move from considering video collection as a format decision to seeing a concrete collection-and-reuse workflow worth evaluating through a free account.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: The single email must establish the product, explain one useful mechanism and earn the signup independently. Video reuse directly serves the selected audience's required format and researched uncertainty about collection and display. It requires no assumed integration or invented failing workflow. The alternative offers a distinct acquisition argument about configuring the video request itself. Neither argument claims to resolve reluctance to ask, student participation, testimonial quality or incentive authenticity.

emails.selection_reason: The selected job requires video, while the research raises collection and display questions. Automatic transcription and widget reuse give this reader a concrete reason to evaluate what happens after a video is submitted.
emails.target_audience: Cohort-based course operators seeking student video testimony for course or cohort sales pages.
emails.job: Earn a free signup to evaluate collecting a student video and reusing that submitted testimony.
emails.single_idea: A student video collected in Senja can also be viewed as transcribed text and used in a website widget, giving the operator concrete reuse options for the same submitted testimony.
emails.felt_need: Where should I collect and display student testimonials?
emails.status_quo: Researched creators report using testimonials on their websites and course or cohort offers. Their collection tools and video workflows are not established.
emails.mechanism: After creating an account and choosing Free, the operator can collect up to 15 video and text testimonials. Once a student submits a video, Senja automatically transcribes it for viewing as text, and the video can be used in a widget. The concrete evaluation is one submitted student video: inspect its transcript and its use in a website widget. Student submission is a prerequisite for evaluating those outputs.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: For an operator whose immediate decision is how to request the required video format, a configurable collection question offers a different reason to begin an evaluation.
alternative_arguments.single_idea: When the next cohort's sales page needs student video testimony, Senja lets the operator explicitly request video rather than leave the response format unspecified.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: Do I ask for video testimonials or just written ones?
alternative_arguments.status_quo: Research records creators using testimonials across websites and course or cohort offers, without establishing how they currently request a particular format.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: After signup, create a collection form and set a question to Video, which requires a recorded or uploaded video answer. A Video and text setting instead lets the student choose one format; it does not collect both for the same question. Free allows collection of 15 video and text testimonials. The initial evaluation is whether this explicit video-request workflow fits the operator's intended ask.

events.body:
Use Senja to collect student video testimonials for your course sales page.

Senja is testimonial collection software: you can request student videos, then use the submitted testimony on your website. For a future cohort launch, that gives you a way to collect and display students’ own words.

Once a student submits a video, Senja automatically transcribes it so you can view it as text too. That same video can go into a website widget.

Sign up and choose Free to collect up to **15 video and text testimonials**. One student submission gives you a concrete evaluation: inspect its transcript and see how the video works in a widget for your course page.

events.subject: Student videos, with transcripts and widgets
events.preview_text: See how submitted student testimony could fit your course sales page.
events.body:
Senja is a testimonial collection tool that automatically transcribes submitted videos.

Once a student submits a video, you can read their testimony as text, too. The video can also go in a website widget on your course sales page.

That gives you a concrete workflow to evaluate before a future cohort launch: collecting student testimony on camera, reviewing its transcript and using the submitted video on your page.

Signup lets you start with Free: one form and up to **15 video and text testimonials** in total. A student’s video submission gives you the material to test the transcription and widget reuse for yourself.

Senja is testimonial collection software for requesting student videos and displaying the responses. For a future cohort launch, the collection starts with a form you share by link.

The context and problem reports below describe observed members of this market, not established experiences or installed tools of this recipient. The campaign request controls which job this email addresses; do not require a link to an unrequested integration in your doubts or click requirements.
Observed context (inferred; applicability must be checked): The corpus supports course creators who collect student feedback for course marketing, including a newly launched creator unsure how to ask and established creators using testimonials on landing pages and course or cohort offers. It does not establish the narrower situation of needing student videos before an imminent cohort launch.
Source: https://www.bmf.io/threads/what-are-the-best-ways-to-collect-testimonials-for-my-online-course.9780/; quote: I just launched my online course, and I know testimonials can help attract more students. The problem is, I don't know how to get them.
Source: https://codewithandrea.com/meta/my-2022-in-review/; quote: With this approach, I collected many great testimonials that I later placed on the course landing page.
Source: https://www.authorcirclehub.com/p/why-testimonials-are-the-most-underrated; quote: I have been collecting testimonials and using them on my Substack publication, my website, and across my offers, such as my course and cohort for the past six months.
Problem context: A newly launched course creator reports not knowing how to obtain testimonials and feeling reluctant to ask for reviews because it could seem pushy. [Source limits: Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.]; source: https://www.bmf.io/threads/what-are-the-best-ways-to-collect-testimonials-for-my-online-course.9780/
Problem context: The same creator is unsure whether incentives would seem fake, whether to request video or written testimonials, and where to collect and display them. [Source limits: Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.]; source: https://www.bmf.io/threads/what-are-the-best-ways-to-collect-testimonials-for-my-online-course.9780/
Problem context: Neera reports that praise does not automatically become strong testimonials: asking appropriately and promptly matters, and delayed requests can produce weaker recollections. [Source limits: Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.]; source: https://www.authorcirclehub.com/p/why-testimonials-are-the-most-underrated
Qualified scope of the selected audience: cohort-based course operators. This narrows who you are; it does not establish installed tools, prior actions or desired reactions.
Reading emphasis: weigh the effort of the next step against its usefulness. Do not assume an installed tool, a switching project or an existing workflow beyond the profile.
readers.what_it_sells: Senja is software that would let me collect student video testimonials through an account-free form, read automatic transcripts, and display the videos on my course sales page.
readers.biggest_doubt: The useful demonstration depends on getting a student to submit a video after I sign up. I understand what happens afterward, but I cannot yet judge what I would be asking the student to do or how much effort it takes.
readers.stopped_at: Signing up gives you a way to evaluate that workflow before your next cohort launch.
fixes: Cut “A student video can go beyond the collection form.” I want the concrete offer immediately.
Expand “Students submit through a personalised form without needing an account or special software.” with a preview of what the student actually sees and is asked to do.

Rewrite “Signing up gives you a way to evaluate that workflow before your next cohort launch.” to explain the first setup step and make the need for a student submission clear before promising an evaluation.
